scope: One synthetic native application-state transfer between two fresh GitHub-hosted jobs; ai-memory2.3.2 and Qdrant1.19.1 only.

provenance.upstream_tests: Ten unchanged ai-memory tests plus four unchanged Qdrant pytest cases. Qdrant tests target the verified release binary, not the upstream debug build; full suites are not claimed.
provenance.upstream_fixture: Unchanged Qdrant basic_collection_setup seeds ten public points.
provenance.local_integration: Existing synthetic memory fixture, exact Restic transfer, full-state and post-restore queries, independent arithmetic oracle and metadata/cleanup guards are our composition.

source_job: Verify selected official archive/executable hashes and fixed upstream revisions.
Run selected unchanged application tests with their own fixtures before transfer preparation.
Run existing unmodified Linux memory runner with corrected frozen oracle; require native backup, same-host calibration restore and all query checks.
Create Qdrant public upstream fixture, city/price indexes and one alias; verify complete points and independently frozen dense/filter/sparse query results.
Create native full-storage snapshot; verify source unchanged; stop only owned application processes.
Encrypt only memory native backup and Qdrant snapshot in one new Restic repository, neutralize native key labels, full-read check, and freeze exact snapshot/archive/ciphertext identities.
destination_job: Use fresh GitHub-hosted job; require distinct boot identity and same workflow run/head plus source output checksum.
Receive exact encrypted source artifact and independently deliver the existing fixture-only Actions secret.
Reject wrong key with no files, check --read-data, restore exact snapshot into an empty owned target, verify both archive hashes.
Native ai-memory restore without force; reopened stdio MCP exact reads, FTS, scope negatives, old-marker absence and no-capture SQLite checks.

Native Qdrant --storage-snapshot without force or storage.temp_path; complete points/config/schema/aliases and real dense/filter/sparse queries via collection and alias equal source and fixed public oracle.
Require unchanged incoming ciphertext and cleanup of owned processes, listeners, runtime and separately supplied password.

key_flow.delivery: Each job receives the existing fixture-only Actions secret separately through a step-scoped environment and writes one new regular0600 private file; native child environments are allowlisted and receive its path only.
uploaded: exact native encrypted app repository in verified text envelope
encrypted raw synthetic command/protocol proof, excluding key or credential files
key_flow.trust_limit: Ciphertext artifacts and separately delivered secret share the same GitHub administrative account.

boundaries.upstream_http_fixture: Unchanged helper binds all addresses inside a separate network namespace containing loopback only; packages are fetched before this phase.
boundaries.providers: No model, embedding or external account route; frozen memory config disables capture/maintenance/providers.

failures: First unsupported native error, refusal, oracle mismatch or cleanup failure ends that phase; record command and streams without unchanged retry. Evidence sealing and owned cleanup still run.
limitations: Synthetic application usability only; no private user database, production recovery, client rebinding, reboot or whole-stack claim.
Exact snapshots created by the source job are frozen before destination execution; this does not retroactively qualify old private app-state archives.
Separate jobs and distinct boot identities support fresh-host separation; no independent administrative trust domain or account-loss recovery claim.
Sequential app snapshots are not one cross-application atomic transaction.
Selected source tests are distinct from the composed cross-host fixture and from actual destination acceptance.
Native applications run with owned paths and filtered environments on disposable runners; no general OS filesystem sandbox claim.
No token-saving claim; provider usage is not measured.
